claims.statement: An external client app has a Consumer Key and an optional Consumer Secret that a developer copies from the app settings after verifying their identity; the secret is needed only where the app specifies that the Web Server Flow requires it.

sources.supports: Depending on whether you’ve specified that it’s required, also copy the Consumer Secret.
sources.locator: Create an External Client App in Your Org: consumer key and secret steps

sources.supports: If you specified in the external client app that the Web Server Flow requires a client (consumer) secret, the command prompts you for it.
sources.locator: Create an External Client App in Your Org: closing paragraphs

claims.statement: Salesforce documents that the token request of the web server flow is a POST with a form-encoded body, that client_secret is a parameter of that body, required unless the external client app does not have Require Secret for Web Server Flow enabled, and that the client id and secret may instead be sent in an HTTP Basic Authorization header (the body wins when both are sent).

sources.supports: client_secret This parameter is required unless the external client app doesn’t have Require Secret for Web Server Flow enabled.
sources.locator: OAuth 2.0 Web Server Flow for Web App Integration, token request parameters

sources.supports: Instead of sending client credentials as parameters in the body of the POST, Salesforce supports the HTTP Basic authentication scheme. This scheme’s format requires the client_id and client_secret in the authorization header of the post as follows:
sources.locator: OAuth 2.0 Web Server Flow for Web App Integration, Basic authentication

sources.supports: Note If the client_id and client_secret are sent in the POST’s body, the authorization header is ignored.
sources.locator: OAuth 2.0 Web Server Flow for Web App Integration, Basic authentication

openQuestions.question: This candidate is recorded at existence level only: the pages read state no prefix, length, alphabet or separator for the consumer secret, and do not say whether a connected app consumer secret has the same or a different shape. Is the connected-app consumer secret a separate family, and what does either look like? One open-source scanner rule artifact (TruffleHog, read 2026-10-04) matches a consumer secret only near a salesforce/consumer/secret keyword; a single artifact does not corroborate, so it stays a lead and no shape is recorded.

The web server flow page names the wire parameter client_secret; the external client app settings page names the Consumer Secret. That the two are the same value is the reading of the two pages and is not stated in one sentence.
Whether a connected app consumer secret is a separate family or the same credential is not stated.
